routes.name: Treaty of Peace and Friendship (India–Nepal, 1950), Article 7

note: India, read on 2026-10-30. The Ministry of External Affairs' page on the services of the Foreigners Regional Registration Offices: a foreign national on a visa valid for more than 180 days registers with the FRRO/FRO within 14 days of arrival, and an employment visa application carries the Indian company's undertaking (so the work is tied to it). The Employment Visa's terms are from the Ministry of Home Affairs' frequently asked questions as reproduced by TaxGuru (secondary; the Ministry's and the Bureau of Immigration's pages refuse this client): granted by an Indian mission abroad for up to a year, the first extension by the Ministry, further ones by the State Government or FRO up to five years from the visa's issue (the year kept as its term, renewable); foreign artists engaged to perform regularly for an employment contract's length are among those it serves. Article 7 of the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship with Nepal, read in the MEA's own copy (rendered in a browser; it is drawn by script), grants each country's nationals the same privileges in residence, property, trade and movement in the other, read as free movement for Nepalese nationals. Fees, decision times, the Overseas Citizen of India card, Bhutan's nationals, and naturalisation's count aren't written.

sources.said: A foreign national who enters India on a visa valid for a stay in India for a period of more than 180 days is required to register with the FRO/FRO concerned within 14 days of arrival in India. ... sources.title: TaxGuru, Business Visa, Employment Visa and the MHA’s Frequently Asked Questions
sources.said: A foreign national coming to India for employment may initially be granted an Employment Visa by the Indian Missions abroad upto one year. The first extension, if necessary, would be granted by MHA. Further extensions, if required, can be granted by concerned State Government/FRO upto maximum period of five years from the date of issue of the Visa. ... Foreign artists engaged to conduct regular performances for the duration of employment contract given by Hotels, clubs etc.

sources.title: Ministry of External Affairs, Treaty of Peace and Friendship between India and Nepal (1950)
sources.said: Article 7 The Governments of India and Nepal agree to grant, on reciprocal basis, to the nationals of one country in the territories o the other the same privileges in the matter of residence, ownership of property, participation in trade and commerce, movement and other privileges of a similar nature.
